messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

The user explicitly says Messi in Euros, so we should use currency=EUR. For LeBron, they want British Pounds, so currency=GBP. Then BMI: first person weight 85 kg, height 180 cm, unit metric. Second person weight 200 pounds, height 6 feet 2 inches, unit imperial. We need to call the functions. The user wants both net worths and BMIs. We can do them sequentially or combine? The user wants all four results. We can call each function separately. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we should call celebrity_net_worth_get twice with appropriate arguments, then calculate_bmi twice. The user wants Messi in Euros, LeBron in GBP. So we call celebrity_net_worth_get for Messi with currency=EUR, name="Lionel Messi". Then for LeBron with currency=GBP, name="LeBron James". Then calculate_bmi for first person weight=85, height=180, unit=metric. Then second person weight=200, height=6 feet 2 inches, unit=imperial. The user didn't specify the unit for the second BMI, but they said "using the imperial system", so we set unit=imperial. The function signature expects weight, height, optional unit. So we pass weight=200, height="6 feet 2 inches", unit=imperial. That should be fine. The user wants the net worth in Euros for Messi, so we set currency=EUR. For LeBron, currency=GBP. The user didn't specify the currency for Messi's net worth, but they said Euros. So we set currency=EUR. The user didn't specify the currency for LeBron's net worth, but they said British Pounds. So we set currency=GBP. So we call the function twice. Then we call calculate_bmi twice.
